headline: Medium risk: Haystack’s broad egress and MCP exposure can leak or misroute outputs, while the sample travel-planning repo adds little direct protection.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so it can ingest external content through shared channels; the Spring Integration samples repo is runnable:false and shows no protective isolation. Because the pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly and no provenance controls are shown, prompt injection is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Haystack is connected to an MCP server that forwards untrusted content into prompts, injection is possible.
IF the Spring Integration samples are used as a message bridge without content filtering, attacker text can reach Haystack.
mitigations: Disable MCP endpoints not needed for the workflow.
Add a strict allowlist for message sources and fields.
Insert a provenance tag check before any prompt assembly.
Use a manual review step for externally sourced text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and schema validation at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress, but the profile only shows anonymous usage statistics as touched data; the Spring Integration samples repo has network_egress:none and no data classes touched. With no shared workspace or sensitive data documented, leakage risk is limited and not evidenced as default.
conditions: IF Haystack is configured to send retrieved documents or prompts to third-party APIs, leakage risk increases.
IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive workspace, data exposure becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep Haystack on local-only retrieval sources.
Do not place secrets in any shared workspace.
Review outbound destinations in Haystack before deployment.
Run the Spring Integration samples offline only.
requires-engineering: segregate workspaces and enforce egress policy at the network layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack advertises broad network egress and MCP/API calls, but the Spring Integration samples repo is runnable:false and has no write or network capabilities exposed in the profile. No overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface is documented, so a capability conflict pathway is not supported.
conditions: IF the Spring Integration samples are wrapped into a writable shared workspace, conflict risk could emerge.
IF both agents are later granted write access to the same mutable resource, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Keep the sample repo read-only.
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Separate networked components from local samples.
Document ownership of any mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state if write access is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can emit retrieved or generated outputs through APIs/MCP, and the Spring Integration samples can be used as an integration layer that may pass those outputs onward. No verification step is documented, so if B consumes A’s text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports.
conditions: IF the Spring Integration samples route Haystack output into another system without validation, cascading errors can propagate.
IF Haystack-generated facts are treated as authoritative by downstream consumers, incorrect outputs can be amplified.
mitigations: Add a verification gate before forwarding any Haystack output.
Require source citations for all generated claims.
Log and review transformed messages before release.
Limit downstream actions to non-destructive operations.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds and human approval for action-taking flows.

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics and has broad egress, while the Spring Integration samples repo shows no data classes or residency-sensitive handling. No specific residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy drift rather than a concrete breach pathway.
conditions: IF EU personal data is routed through Haystack to a US-only service, residency concerns arise.
IF either agent is configured to retain logs beyond policy, retention mismatch becomes relevant.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through Haystack.
Check logging and retention settings before use.
Keep the sample repo free of personal data.
Document data-flow boundaries for the pair.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls.
